$comment: Lighthouse CI — the synthetic speed gate on the PR's own Vercel preview (ADR-930, tuned ADR-936).
WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not a measurement of the Core Web Vitals budgets in
lib/analytics/vitals-budgets.ts. Those are FIELD p75 numbers from real visitors on real
devices, scored by the vitals_p75 RPC. This is a LAB run on a shared GitHub runner
against a cold preview deployment. The two are different instruments and gating field
budgets on lab numbers would be a category error.
WHAT IT IS: a regression smoke alarm. Every threshold below sits ABOVE the marketing field
budget (LCP 2000ms / CLS 0.1), so passing here means 'nothing collapsed', not 'we met the
budget'. A PR that doubles the JS on a marketing page or drops a render-blocking font trips
it; a PR that costs 80ms does not, and should not, because the run cannot resolve 80ms.
INP IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE. It needs a real interaction from a real person, so Lighthouse
cannot produce one. Total Blocking Time is the lab stand-in and is asserted instead.
Anyone reading a green tick here should not conclude the INP budget is met -- only the
field data in the insights Experience tab can say that.
numberOfRuns 3 + median: a single lab run on shared CI is too noisy to gate on.
The URLs are the ONE-PER-SHAPE set, not everything: the home PhotoHero (the heaviest
LCP on the site), a dense product page, a Puck-rendered template, and an SEO guide.
── THE MEASURED BASELINE (run 30934494633, 2026-08-04, 4 URLs x 3 runs, medians) ────────
URL              LCP     CLS     TBT    FCP     Weight
/pricing         941ms   0.032    1ms   404ms   1.21MB
/the-community   916ms   0.032    2ms   459ms   1.15MB
/loneliness      950ms   0.032    0ms   419ms   1.18MB
ADR-930 shipped the first thresholds as admitted guesses (LCP 4000 / CLS 0.1 / TBT 600)
and said to re-set them from real data. This is that re-set. The guesses were far looser
than the site: LCP had 4.2x headroom and TBT had SIXTY-SIX times. A gate with 66x headroom
cannot fail, and a gate that cannot fail is decoration.
How each number below was chosen, and why not tighter:
LCP 2500  — worst median 950ms. Cannot go below 2000: that is the marketing FIELD budget,
and a lab gate stricter than the field target would fail PRs for pages that
are fine for real visitors. 2500 is the tightest value that keeps the rule.
CLS 0.10  — worst median 0.032, but 0.1 IS the field budget and the industry good/needs-
improvement boundary, so it is held rather than tightened. No second, tighter
WARN is paired with it: lighthouse-ci takes ONE assertion per audit id, so a
0.05 warn would REPLACE this error, not sit under it.
bounded by the lab convention instead: 300ms is Lighthouse's own needs-
improvement line. Still 33x the worst observed.
FCP 1000  — worst median 459ms. Warn, not error: FCP is a diagnostic for a failing LCP,
not a goal (vitals-budgets.ts says so), so it should inform, never block.
Weight 2MB— worst median 1.23MB. Warn. Deliberately not 1.5MB: a legitimate hero image
swap can move 300KB, and that is not a regression.
THREE WARNS FIRE ON ALL FOUR URLS, identically across all 3 runs:
unused-javascript        0     (the floor -- worst possible score, on every page)
render-blocking-resources 0.5
uses-responsive-images   0.5   (0 on /loneliness)
They stay warns on purpose: they describe payload SHAPE, not a regression. They do not get
worse PR to PR, they are simply always wrong, so an error assertion would fail every PR for
debt none of them created. Recorded as real work in ADR-934, not laundered into a budget.
